admission.justification: StepDot.tsx discloses cached major/child detail, pageParts.tsx binds that data to the matching compact mark and taskBlocks.tsx supplies the pointer-independent nested reading surface, so compact marks do not cost access to sub-step information.

applicability: Major-step dots wherever the task’s step marks are drawn, together with the task-page nested step list as the non-pointer reading surface.
conditions: Pointer rest reveals the supplied major title and display state plus ordered child titles and states, without a new request.
A major with no children shows title and state alone.
Dots add no keyboard focus stop; the task-page nested list retains the same information.
exclusions: Rows that render a progress bar instead of dots.

evidence: Parent examination of actual F01 changed extents; no new execution or acceptance.

statement: Resting the pointer on a major-step dot displays the existing row-held title, state and ordered child states without a request or keyboard focus stop, while task-page step lists provide the same information without a pointer.
